source.title: Causal Dimensionality of Transformer Representations: Measurement, Scaling, and Layer Structure

record.file_problem: The full paper is present. Some equations and figures are flattened in the text, but the reported results are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures SAE feature counts and recovery, and reports that its AtP measure does not recover a causal basis and that current SAE widths under-sample the causal feature set. These results refine or limit claims about SAE features as complete, canonical units; the study does not directly test toy-model superposition geometry.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results on SAE feature counts, causal-feature recovery, decoder geometry, and feature firing sparsity. Rows below cover results relevant to V4 and V5. The sparsity-correlation and geometric-privilege findings are recorded under fits_no_version because they do not directly test a listed claim version. Cited results from other work and values used only for calibration are not recorded as findings.
record.test_reason: The study's main test bears on V5's completeness claim. On Gemma-2-2B layer 12 it sweeps matched-L0 SAE widths from 16k to 1M. The count of causally active features keeps growing, dips from feature splitting at 65k, and reaches only about 72% of a fitted saturation (κ̂≈1,990) at 1M. The authors say current widths are 'substantially under-sampled' for complete causal enumeration. The other experiments (SVA recall, encoder/decoder ablation, synthetic recovery) mainly validate or diagnose the study's own AtP measure. They are not tests of a claim version.
record.authors_conclusion: Partly right. The authors define causal dimensionality κ and estimate κ̂≈1,990 (κ̂/d≈0.77–0.86) on Gemma-2-2B layer 12. They find it is recovered sub-linearly by SAE width, with current widths under-sampled for complete causal enumeration. They also report shape invariance across 2B/9B and a 20× attribution-threshold drop across depth. They argue AtP counts consequential activation patterns routed through the decoder rather than recovering a causal basis, and that the trained encoder is mainly a sparsity filter. The record's emphasis on task-specific recall overstates what is only a validation of their method.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses SAE width sweeps, attribution patching, causal-feature recall, and encoder/decoder ablations to study causal dimensionality. It does not reproduce the original toy-model superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported outcomes depend on SAE width and feature-splitting behavior, AtP threshold, prompt distribution, SAE architecture, and L0 matching. The task-specific recall differs sharply between rc_train and Pile-10k.

fits_no_version.finding: AtP-ranked SAE features on Pythia-70m recover the Marks et al. 56-feature SVA set at 42.9% (p99), 76.8% (p98) and 98.2% (p95) on rc_train, but only 0.04 on Pile-10k.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Attribution-patching scores on SAE features rank a known task circuit's features highly on the task distribution only.

fits_no_version.finding: Replacing the trained encoder with a random projection inflates Ncausal 9.27×. Random or shuffled decoders reduce it.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The trained SAE encoder acts mainly as a sparsity filter for AtP-based causal counts.

fits_no_version.finding: Causal features show about zero gap from magnitude-matched controls in decoder magnitude and mean cosine.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Causally active SAE features are not geometrically distinguishable in decoder space (Gemma-2-2B L12).

fits_no_version.finding: Firing probability vs causal membership: global Spearman ρ=0.24; ρ from −0.70 to −0.10 for gated, p_anneal and standard SAEs; ρ=+0.74 for TopK.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In continuous-activation SAEs, rarer-firing features are more likely to be causal.

fits_no_version.finding: Causal count at 16k is identical (328) for Gemma-2-2B and 9B, but by calibration construction. The cross-threshold count is 336 and inert fractions match. The attribution threshold drops 20× from layer 1 to 23.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The shape of the AtP score distribution is invariant to model scale at matched relative depth.

record.problems: The fitted κ̂ has a wide Wald CI and is based on four post-minimum width points; the authors treat it as an order-of-magnitude estimate. The scale-invariance claim uses one 9B SAE width point. AtP is a first-order proxy, with global activation-patching correlation ρ=0.838, although the reported top-5% correlation exceeds 0.95. The task-specific recall result is distribution- and threshold-dependent; p92 and below are vacuous because ε=0. The paper states that code is not yet public.
record.rows_left_out: No rows were omitted for the 60-row limit. R17–R20 are referenced under fits_no_version and describe findings not assigned to a listed version.

untested.parts: No test of toy-model superposition geometry, phase transition or near-orthogonality. The only toy model is used to check AtP recovery.
No measure of neuron polysemanticity or capacity allocation.
No measure of features spread across neurons, and no clean test of SAE recovery of sparse features. The SVA recall and synthetic results concern the AtP selection method.
Not tested: stability across seeds or runs, canonicality across SAEs, or completeness for non-causal (representational) features. Only the causal coverage of SAE widths is tested.

missing.what: Canonical (non-matched-L0) GemmaScope sweep: Ncausal [328, 407, 731, 4516, 13960, 28801], exceeding d=2304. The authors attribute this to an L0 confound and multiple features clearing ε along the same causal direction. This bears on V5 (features not canonical; split features).

Wedge between representational and causal counts: Nrepr grows 15.6× (15,973→249,566) while Ncausal grows 4.35×, bootstrap CI [3.86, 4.91]. Robust across thresholds (4.0–4.7×) and across TopK, JumpReLU and standard SAEs (1.32–1.56× over 16× width).

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked the SVA recall rows to V4 and labelled them supports/limits_scope. Those rows validate the study's AtP threshold against another SAE-derived feature set, so they are relinked to none. The synthetic zero-recall result (R16) is ambiguous about which features were scored, and the authors read it as a property of AtP. The reader's 'challenges' label on V5 from R16 is therefore dropped. R6 is fixed by calibration. The fits_no_version entries referenced nonexistent rows R17–R20; those references are cleared. Single-SAE-per-width design, a preprint, and no public code.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test toy networks with more sparse features than dimensions, overlap between feature directions, near-orthogonality, or a sparsity-dependent superposition transition.
It does not measure neuron polysemanticity or test whether important features get dedicated dimensions while others share capacity.
It does not test whether polysemantic neurons arise without capacity pressure.
The SAE recovery test concerns a task-specific SVA circuit on Pythia-70m, not feature spreading across neurons or broad recovery of general model features.
The study tests causal-feature recovery and width-dependent causal coverage, not whether SAE features are stable across training runs or canonical units of all model representations.
It does not test whether represented features are one-dimensional or multidimensional.

rows.note: The paper describes this as a non-trivial threshold.
rows.check: This is a validation of the study's own AtP threshold against the Marks et al. SVA feature set, which is itself made of SAE features. It measures how well AtP ranks features, not whether SAEs recover sparse features (V4).

rows.note: The paper says these cuts are vacuous and should not be interpreted as meaningful recovery.
rows.check: Vacuous cut: ε=0 selects all 32,768 features. This is a threshold artefact and should not be a result row.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2B
rows.operation_detail: Measured the number of SAE features above the fixed AtP threshold in the matched-L0 width sweep.
rows.note: Reference-width threshold calibration sets this count to approximately 2% of width; it is not independent evidence of completeness.
rows.check: The 328 at the reference width is fixed by construction: ε is calibrated to the 98th percentile, so the count is 2% of width. It carries no evidence on its own.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2B
rows.operation_detail: Measured Ncausal after replacing the trained encoder with a random orthonormal projection while retaining the trained decoder.
rows.note: The authors interpret the trained encoder as a sparsity filter that suppresses background features, rather than as a feature selector.
rows.check: An encoder ablation diagnosing what AtP/Ncausal measures. It does not measure whether SAE features are complete or canonical units.

rows.note: The control replaces the trained decoder with a random orthonormal matrix.

rows.subject: toy model (R64, 500 features, 50 causal)
rows.operation_detail: Compared SAE features with ground-truth causal directions using cosine-threshold recovery.
rows.value: identically zero across all 24 runs at all listed cosine thresholds
rows.note: The authors conclude that AtP measures activation patterns routed through the decoder and does not recover a causal basis.
rows.check: The text is ambiguous about which features were scored: all SAE decoder directions, or only AtP-selected ones. The authors read zero recall as showing what AtP measures, not as SAEs failing to learn features. SAE training details are absent, so this cannot ground a challenge.

relationships.condition: Gemma-2-2B layer 12, matched-L0 GemmaScope SAEs, widths 32k–1M, AtP threshold fixed at reference width
relationships.reason: Causal feature count keeps rising with width (240→1,427), dips at 65k from splitting, and reaches only about 72% of fitted κ̂ at 1M. So no tested SAE is a complete causal enumeration (R7–R12).
relationships.display_finding: The number of causally relevant features rose from 240 to 1,427 with width, dipped at 65k from splitting, and reached only about 72% of the fitted κ̂ at 1M, so no tested SAE enumerated all causal features.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.reason: SVA recall falls to 0.04 on the wrong distribution, so the recovery result depends on the prompt distribution (R4).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Gemma-2-2B layer 12, matched-L0 SAE width sweep
reader_labels.reason: Ncausal changes with SAE width, includes a reported dip, and reaches 1,427 at width 1,048,576 versus a fitted κ̂≈1,990; the paper describes current widths as under-sampled for complete causal enumeration (R6–R12).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Synthetic ground-truth causal-direction recovery across 24 toy-model SAE runs
reader_labels.reason: Recall of ground-truth causal directions is identically zero at the tested cosine thresholds; the authors state that AtP does not recover a causal basis (R16).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Gemma-2-2B layer 12 encoder/decoder ablation at width 16,384
reader_labels.reason: The encoder ablation inflates Ncausal to 9.27× the real value, while decoder controls reduce it; this supports the authors’ narrower account of the encoder as a sparsity filter rather than a feature selector (R13–R15).
